# Correctness

**PASS.** A published smooth K3 surface has rank-20 Néron–Severi generated by 60 explicitly specified lines. The supplied verifier reconstructs the full orbit and the F4-Frobenius permutation, and gives two exact modular rank lower bounds 10 and 10 for the plus and minus algebraic eigenspaces. Nondegeneracy and published Picard rank 20 force equality. Complete enumeration of every projective point over F4 and F16 gives exactly 20 and 554 points, hence by the K3 trace formula the two unknown Frobenius eigenvalues have trace 3 and determinant 16. This reconstructs the degree-22 Weil polynomial, not just a numerical pattern. Computation uses the actual self-contained VERIFY.py.

# Originality

**PASS, with residual risk.** Rams–Schütt supply the quartic, explicit line, group orbit and Picard rank, but their Section 8 does not calculate the F4 Frobenius characteristic polynomial, the two finite-field point counts or the zeta function. Degtyarev describes complete *geometric* large-line configurations and the complex quartic classification is not arithmetic over F4. The known data yield a 20-dimensional algebraic subrepresentation only after its Frobenius action is computed; the two-dimensional remaining factor is not fixed by the Néron–Severi lattice and requires new arithmetic point-count input. Targeted searches of the scientific literature and published mathematical-result database did not find a dominating arithmetic computation. Later specialized literature remains a possible source of duplication, and a 2020 Warwick thesis was not readable in full.

# Value

**PASS.** The complete zeta function is a natural arithmetic invariant of the record 60-line smooth quartic over F4. It determines *every* extension-field point count, exposes an irreducible rank-two Frobenius factor with discriminant -55, and separates geometric line-class information from genuinely arithmetic transcendental cohomology. Neither the published 60-line count nor the Néron–Severi discriminant gives those full point counts. This is a substantive complete calculation on a distinguished arithmetic K3 surface rather than an isolated ad hoc check.

# Closest literature and limitations

Rams–Schütt, arXiv:1512.01358 (Section 8) establish the object and its geometric Picard span. Degtyarev, arXiv:1604.05836 (Remark 8.10), treats geometric large-line configurations. Degtyarev–Itenberg–Sertöz, arXiv:1601.04238, classify characteristic-zero quartics, so their rationality and geometry are not the F4 Frobenius calculation. A thesis by Broggi on K3 Picard groups over finite fields was identified, but its complete text could not be inspected; it remains a residual duplication risk. The claim is restricted to the displayed F4 model, with exactly checked finite arithmetic and a standard K3 trace argument. No claim of independent validation is made.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
